acid-base-titration.title: Acid-Base Neutralization Titration
acid-base-titration.description: Standardized hydrochloric acid is used to titrate a sodium hydroxide solution of unknown concentration, with phenolphthalein as the indicator to determine the endpoint. Students develop the fundamental skills of quantitative analysis.
objectives: Understand the principle of neutralization titration and how to identify the endpoint
Use a burette correctly and safely
Calculate the unknown concentration from titration data

hcl-naoh-neutralization.title: Measurement of Neutralization Enthalpy for Hydrochloric Acid and Sodium Hydroxide
hcl-naoh-neutralization.description: The enthalpy of neutralization for the reaction between hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide solution is determined using an insulated cup calorimeter, illustrating the energy change associated with an exothermic reaction.
objectives: Determine the enthalpy of neutralization experimentally
Understand the energy changes in an exothermic reaction
Identify and analyze potential sources of experimental error

indicator-color-change.title: Color Change Behavior of Acid-Base Indicators
indicator-color-change.description: The color changes of litmus, phenolphthalein, and methyl orange in acidic and alkaline solutions are observed and recorded, and the transition ranges of each indicator are established.
objectives: Become familiar with common acid-base indicators
Understand the color transition ranges of each indicator
Use indicator color to determine whether a solution is acidic or alkaline

vinegar-soda.title: Reaction of Vinegar with Baking Soda
vinegar-soda.description: Students investigate the reaction between household vinegar (acetic acid) and baking soda, observing the evolution of carbon dioxide and connecting laboratory chemistry to everyday experience.
objectives: Observe the reaction between a weak acid and a hydrogen carbonate salt
Recognize the conditions under which carbon dioxide is produced
Relate the observed reaction to a familiar real-life context

metal-oxide-acid.title: Reaction of Copper(II) Oxide with Dilute Sulfuric Acid
metal-oxide-acid.description: Black copper(II) oxide is dissolved in dilute sulfuric acid to yield a blue copper(II) sulfate solution. The experiment illustrates the general reaction between a basic oxide and an acid.
objectives: Understand the reaction of a basic oxide with an acid
Observe the color change of the solution during the reaction
Write and balance the corresponding chemical equation

limewater-co2.title: Reaction of Carbon Dioxide with Limewater
limewater-co2.description: Carbon dioxide is bubbled through clear limewater, causing it to turn milky. The experiment establishes the standard laboratory test for carbon dioxide.
objectives: Master the laboratory test for CO₂
Understand the reaction between an alkali and an acidic oxide
Observe the formation of a precipitate

carbonate-acid-identify.title: Identification of Carbonate Salts
carbonate-acid-identify.description: Dilute hydrochloric acid is used to identify solid sodium carbonate: the gas evolved turns limewater milky, confirming the presence of the carbonate ion.
objectives: Master the test for the carbonate ion
Observe gas evolution as evidence of a chemical reaction
Connect the procedure to the principles of qualitative analysis

ph-measurement.title: Measurement of pH in Common Solutions
ph-measurement.description: The pH of several everyday solutions is measured using both pH paper and a pH meter. The two methods are compared with respect to accuracy and practical convenience.
objectives: Master the use of pH paper and a pH meter
Understand the relationship between pH and the acidic or alkaline character of a solution
Compare the precision of the two measurement methods

weak-acid-ionization.title: Ionization of Weak Electrolytes
weak-acid-ionization.description: Compare the electrical conductivity and pH of hydrochloric acid and acetic acid at equal concentrations to understand the partial ionization characteristic of weak electrolytes.
objectives: Distinguish between strong and weak electrolytes
Understand ionization equilibrium
Explain differences in electrical conductivity

salt-hydrolysis.title: Investigation of Salt Hydrolysis
salt-hydrolysis.description: Measure the pH of sodium carbonate, ammonium chloride, and sodium chloride solutions to investigate the pattern by which salt hydrolysis renders a solution acidic or basic.
objectives: Understand the principles of salt hydrolysis
Determine the acidity or basicity of salt solutions
Write hydrolysis equations

antacid-stomach.title: Investigation of Antacid Neutralization of Stomach Acid
antacid-stomach.description: Use antacids such as aluminium hydroxide and sodium bicarbonate to neutralize dilute hydrochloric acid as a model of gastric acid, and connect the observations to acid–base neutralization in medicine.
objectives: Understand the mechanism of antacid drugs
Observe the neutralization process
Make connections to medical applications

diprotic-acid-titration.title: Titration of a Diprotic Strong Acid
diprotic-acid-titration.description: Titrate sulfuric acid with sodium hydroxide and use the resulting pH curve to recognize that the two ionization stages of a diprotic strong acid are neutralized almost simultaneously, producing a single sharp inflection point; compare this behavior with the stepwise titration of phosphoric acid.
objectives: Construct a titration curve
Understand polyprotic acids
Calculate concentration

buffer-solution.title: Properties of Buffer Solutions
buffer-solution.description: Prepare an acetic acid–sodium acetate buffer and test the stability of its pH upon addition of small amounts of acid or base to understand the buffering action.
objectives: Understand the principles of buffering
Test pH stability
Connect buffering to blood chemistry

co2-preparation.title: Laboratory Preparation of Carbon Dioxide
co2-preparation.description: Prepare carbon dioxide by reacting marble (calcium carbonate) with dilute hydrochloric acid, and become proficient with gas-generation and gas-collection apparatus.
objectives: Master the principle of CO₂ preparation
Learn the upward displacement of air collection method
Identify CO₂

o2-from-h2o2.title: Preparation of Oxygen from Hydrogen Peroxide
o2-from-h2o2.description: Decompose hydrogen peroxide using manganese(IV) oxide as a catalyst to generate oxygen, and understand the role of a catalyst.
objectives: Master the preparation of oxygen
Understand the function of a catalyst
Learn the water displacement collection method

h2-from-zinc.title: Preparation of Hydrogen Gas from Zinc and Dilute Sulfuric Acid
h2-from-zinc.description: React zinc granules with dilute sulfuric acid to generate hydrogen gas, verify its combustibility, and perform the squeaky-pop test.
objectives: Master the preparation of hydrogen gas
Test the purity of hydrogen gas
Observe the squeaky-pop phenomenon

nh3-preparation.title: Preparation of Ammonia Gas and the Fountain Experiment
nh3-preparation.description: Ammonia gas is prepared by heating ammonium chloride with slaked lime, and the classic fountain experiment is performed to demonstrate its exceptionally high solubility in water.
objectives: Master the preparation of ammonia gas
Understand the principle of the fountain experiment
Test for the presence of ammonia gas

so2-preparation.title: Preparation and Properties of Sulfur Dioxide
so2-preparation.description: Sulfur dioxide is prepared by reacting sodium sulfite with sulfuric acid, and its bleaching ability and reducing properties are subsequently verified.
objectives: Master the preparation of SO₂
Verify its bleaching property
Recognize its role as an environmental pollutant

h2s-preparation.title: Preparation and Detection of Hydrogen Sulfide
h2s-preparation.description: Hydrogen sulfide is prepared by reacting iron(II) sulfide with dilute hydrochloric acid; its characteristic rotten-egg odour and strong reducing properties are examined (adequate ventilation required).
objectives: Master the preparation of H₂S
Recognize its toxicity
Understand its reducing property

co2-baking-soda.title: Thermal Decomposition of Sodium Bicarbonate and Gas Evolution Comparison
co2-baking-soda.description: The gas evolved when sodium bicarbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid is compared with other reactions, illustrating the chemical basis for sodium bicarbonate's use as a leavening agent.
objectives: Observe the gas evolution phenomena
Connect the chemistry to everyday applications
Test for carbon dioxide

ammonia-fountain-hcl.title: White Smoke Formation from Ammonia Gas and Hydrogen Chloride
ammonia-fountain-hcl.description: A glass stirring rod moistened with concentrated aqueous ammonia is brought close to one moistened with concentrated hydrochloric acid; the white smoke of ammonium chloride that forms illustrates gas-phase reactions between volatile compounds.
objectives: Observe the white smoke phenomenon
Understand reactions between gases
Recognize the formation of ammonium chloride

carbonate-thermal.title: Investigation of the Thermal Decomposition of Ammonium Bicarbonate
carbonate-thermal.description: Ammonium bicarbonate is heated and observed to decompose completely into ammonia gas, water vapour, and carbon dioxide, illustrating the thermal instability characteristic of ammonium salts.
objectives: Observe the gases produced upon decomposition
Test for ammonia gas and CO₂
Recognize the thermal instability of ammonium salts

co2-properties.title: Investigation of the Properties of Carbon Dioxide
co2-properties.description: Carbon dioxide is shown to be incapable of supporting combustion and to be denser than air; its reaction with water to form carbonic acid is confirmed by the colour change of litmus to red.
objectives: Identify the properties of CO₂
Verify its reaction with water
Connect its properties to fire-extinguishing applications

o2-properties.title: Investigation of the Properties of Oxygen
o2-properties.description: A glowing wooden splint, iron wire, and sulfur powder are used to verify that oxygen supports combustion, and vigorous burning phenomena are observed in each case.
objectives: Recognize that oxygen supports combustion
Observe the combustion of iron wire in oxygen
Distinguish between a substance that supports combustion and one that is combustible

chlorine-preparation.title: Laboratory Preparation of Chlorine
chlorine-preparation.description: Chlorine is generated by heating manganese(IV) oxide with concentrated hydrochloric acid; its bleaching effect and irritating properties are then verified (all operations conducted in a fume hood).
objectives: Master the laboratory preparation of chlorine
Verify the bleaching properties of chlorine
Understand the necessity of tail-gas treatment

agcl-precipitation.title: Detection of Chloride Ions
agcl-precipitation.description: Silver nitrate solution is added dropwise to sodium chloride solution, producing a white precipitate that is insoluble in dilute nitric acid, thereby confirming the presence of chloride ions.
objectives: Master the method for detecting chloride ions
Observe the formation of the white precipitate
Understand the conditions for double-decomposition reactions

baso4-precipitation.title: Detection of Sulfate Ions
baso4-precipitation.description: Barium chloride solution is used to test for sulfate ions in sodium sulfate solution, yielding a white barium sulfate precipitate that is insoluble in acid.
objectives: Master the method for detecting sulfate ions
Eliminate interference from other ions
Observe the characteristics of the precipitate

cuoh2-precipitation.title: Preparation of Copper(II) Hydroxide
cuoh2-precipitation.description: Copper(II) sulfate solution reacts with sodium hydroxide to form a blue, flocculent copper(II) hydroxide precipitate; the characteristic appearance of the precipitate is observed and recorded.
objectives: Prepare copper(II) hydroxide by precipitation
Observe the blue flocculent precipitate
Write the corresponding ionic equation

feoh3-precipitation.title: Preparation of Iron(III) Hydroxide
feoh3-precipitation.description: Iron(III) chloride solution reacts with sodium hydroxide to produce a reddish-brown iron(III) hydroxide precipitate, illustrating the characteristic behaviour of iron in the +3 oxidation state.
objectives: Prepare iron(III) hydroxide by precipitation
Observe the reddish-brown precipitate
Distinguish between the +2 and +3 oxidation states of iron

caco3-precipitation.title: Formation of Calcium Carbonate
caco3-precipitation.description: Sodium carbonate solution reacts with calcium chloride solution to form a white calcium carbonate precipitate, providing a context for understanding the conversion of sparingly soluble salts.
objectives: Observe the formation of the precipitate
Understand the principle of double decomposition
Relate the reaction to the formation of scale in hard water

mgoh2-precipitation.title: Preparation of Magnesium Hydroxide
mgoh2-precipitation.description: Magnesium chloride reacts with sodium hydroxide to produce a white magnesium hydroxide precipitate, illustrating the preparation of a sparingly soluble base.
objectives: Prepare magnesium hydroxide by precipitation
Observe the white precipitate
Connect the reaction to the industrial extraction of magnesium from seawater

agi-precipitation.title: Silver Iodide Precipitation and Cloud Seeding
agi-precipitation.description: Silver nitrate reacts with potassium iodide to form a yellow silver iodide precipitate; the application of silver iodide as a cloud-seeding agent in artificial rainfall is discussed.
objectives: Observe the formation of the yellow precipitate
Compare the colours of the silver halide precipitates
Connect the chemistry to a real-world application

agbr-precipitation.title: Silver Bromide Precipitation and Photosensitive Materials
agbr-precipitation.description: Silver nitrate reacts with potassium bromide to form a pale yellow silver bromide precipitate; this experiment examines its photosensitivity and the underlying principles of photography.
objectives: Observe the formation of a pale yellow precipitate
Understand the photosensitive properties of silver bromide
Connect the reaction to film-based photographic technology

precipitation-conversion.title: Conversion of Precipitates
precipitation-conversion.description: Adding iron(III) chloride solution to a magnesium hydroxide precipitate converts the white solid to a reddish-brown precipitate, illustrating the concept of the solubility product.
objectives: Understand the principle of precipitate conversion
Recognise the relative magnitudes of solubility products
Analyse the direction in which conversion proceeds

hard-water-softening.title: Softening of Hard Water
hard-water-softening.description: Adding sodium carbonate to hard water causes calcium and magnesium ions to precipitate, demonstrating the harmful effects of hard water and the methods used to soften it.
objectives: Identify the ionic composition of hard water
Understand the chemical principle of water softening
Compare the properties of hard and soft water

baso4-gravimetric.title: Gravimetric Determination of Sulfate Content Using Barium Sulfate
baso4-gravimetric.description: Sulfate ions are precipitated with barium chloride; the precipitate is filtered, washed, ignited, and weighed to determine the sulfate content of the sample.
objectives: Master the procedure of gravimetric analysis
Carry out precipitation washing according to standard technique
Calculate sulfate content from mass data

double-decomposition-rule.title: Conditions for Double Decomposition Reactions
double-decomposition-rule.description: By examining several reactions between salts and bases, and between two salts, students deduce that a double decomposition reaction proceeds only when a precipitate, a gas, or water is formed.
objectives: Summarise the conditions required for double decomposition
Compare outcomes with and without precipitate formation
Write net ionic equations for the reactions

kmno4-oxalic-acid.title: Oxidation of Oxalic Acid by Potassium Permanganate
kmno4-oxalic-acid.description: The purple colour of acidic potassium permanganate is discharged upon reaction with oxalic acid; this experiment investigates the effects of concentration and temperature on the reaction rate.
objectives: Observe the decolourisation caused by oxidation
Understand the strong oxidising character of potassium permanganate
Investigate factors that affect the rate of reaction

kmno4-fe2.title: Titration of Iron(II) with Potassium Permanganate
kmno4-fe2.description: A standard potassium permanganate solution is used to titrate iron(II) sulfate; the endpoint is taken when the purple colour persists, illustrating the technique of redox titration.
objectives: Master the technique of redox titration
Use the self-indicating property of potassium permanganate to identify the endpoint
Calculate the iron(II) content from titration data

halogen-displacement-cl-br.title: Displacement of Bromine by Chlorine
halogen-displacement-cl-br.description: Passing chlorine into a potassium bromide solution displaces bromine, which imparts an orange colour to the solution, confirming the relative oxidising strengths of the halogens.
objectives: Verify the relative reactivity of the halogens
Observe the separation of layers during solvent extraction
Write net ionic equations for the displacement reaction

halogen-displacement-br-i.title: Displacement of Iodine by Bromine
halogen-displacement-br-i.description: Bromine water is added to a potassium iodide solution, displacing iodine, which is confirmed by the blue coloration with starch; the relative oxidizing strengths of bromine and iodine are thereby compared.
objectives: Verify the relative reactivity of bromine and iodine
Observe the iodine–starch color reaction
Understand the pattern of halogen displacement reactions

iodine-starch.title: Iodine–Starch Color Reaction
iodine-starch.description: The characteristic blue-black color produced when iodine contacts starch is observed; this reaction is used for the detection of iodine and as an endpoint indicator in iodometric titrations.
objectives: Observe the characteristic blue-black coloration
Understand the mechanism of the color reaction
Apply the reaction in quantitative analysis

so2-bromine-water.title: Decolorization of Bromine Water by Sulfur Dioxide
so2-bromine-water.description: Sulfur dioxide is bubbled into bromine water, causing the orange color to fade; this demonstrates that the reaction proceeds by the reducing action of sulfur dioxide rather than by bleaching.
objectives: Recognize the reducing property of SO₂
Distinguish between reduction and bleaching
Write the corresponding chemical equation

h2o2-ki-catalysis.title: Catalytic Decomposition of Hydrogen Peroxide by Iodide Ion
h2o2-ki-catalysis.description: Potassium iodide catalyzes the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide to release oxygen; the catalyst is observed to remain chemically unchanged at the end of the reaction.
objectives: Understand catalytic decomposition
Test for the oxygen produced
Recognize the characteristics of a catalyst

copper-nitric-acid.title: Reaction of Copper with Nitric Acid
copper-nitric-acid.description: Copper reacts with dilute nitric acid to yield a blue solution and a colorless gas that turns brown on contact with air, illustrating the strong oxidizing property of nitric acid (carry out in a fume hood).
objectives: Recognize the oxidizing property of nitric acid
Observe gas evolution and the color change of the solution
Understand why hydrogen is not produced

fe3-reduction-by-iron.title: Reduction of Iron(III) Ions by Iron
fe3-reduction-by-iron.description: Iron powder is added to an iron(III) chloride solution; the yellow-brown color fades to pale green as iron reduces Fe³⁺ to Fe²⁺, confirming the existence of the intermediate oxidation state.
objectives: Understand the intermediate oxidation state of iron
Observe the accompanying color change
Write the corresponding ionic equation

kmno4-ethanol.title: Oxidation of Ethanol by Potassium Permanganate
kmno4-ethanol.description: Acidified potassium permanganate oxidizes ethanol, causing the purple-red color to discharge; the reducing property of alcohols and the nature of the oxidation products are examined.
objectives: Observe the decolorization caused by oxidation
Recognize that alcohols can be oxidized
Relate the reaction to the principle of breath-alcohol testing

iodine-clock.title: Iodine Clock Reaction
iodine-clock.description: Hydrogen peroxide oxidizes potassium iodide to produce iodine, which is continuously reduced back by sodium thiosulfate; once the sodium thiosulfate is consumed, iodine accumulates rapidly and turns the solution suddenly blue in the presence of starch, illustrating the concept of an induction period and the dependence of reaction rate on concentration.
objectives: Observe the iodine clock phenomenon
Understand the concept of an induction period
Investigate the effect of concentration on reaction rate

chlorine-bleaching.title: Bleaching Action of Chlorine Water
chlorine-bleaching.description: Chlorine water is used to decolorize colored cloth strips or fuchsin solution, demonstrating the strong oxidizing power of hypochlorous acid and the underlying bleaching mechanism.
objectives: Understand the principle of bleaching by hypochlorous acid
Distinguish between the roles of chlorine and hypochlorous acid
Connect the experiment to the bleaching action of bleaching powder

fe2-fe3-conversion.title: Interconversion of Two Oxidation States of Iron
fe2-fe3-conversion.description: Chlorine water is used to oxidize Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺, and iron powder is used to reduce Fe³⁺ back to Fe²⁺, illustrating the variable-valence behavior of iron.
objectives: Understand the interconversion of iron oxidation states
Verify the conversions using color change reactions
Write balanced redox equations for each transformation

metal-activity-acid.title: Investigation of the Metal Activity Series
metal-activity-acid.description: The vigor of hydrogen gas evolution when magnesium, zinc, and iron react separately with dilute hydrochloric acid is compared, and the metals are ranked according to their reactivity.
objectives: Compare the relative vigor of each metal's reaction
Rank the three metals in order of decreasing activity
Collect and identify the hydrogen gas produced

iron-copper-sulfate.title: Displacement of Copper from Copper(II) Sulfate by Iron
iron-copper-sulfate.description: An iron nail is immersed in copper(II) sulfate solution; a red copper deposit forms on the nail surface while the blue color of the solution fades, providing evidence for a displacement reaction.
objectives: Observe the characteristic phenomena of the displacement reaction
Understand the difference in activity between iron and copper
Write the ionic and overall chemical equations

copper-silver-nitrate.title: Displacement of Silver from Silver Nitrate Solution by Copper
copper-silver-nitrate.description: A copper wire is placed in silver nitrate solution; a silver-white «silver tree» crystallizes on the wire surface and the solution gradually turns blue, illustrating displacement and crystal growth.
objectives: Observe the growth of the silver tree on the copper wire
Understand the mechanism of the displacement reaction
Account for the blue coloration that develops in the solution

sodium-water.title: Reaction of Sodium with Water
sodium-water.description: Sodium metal is added to water containing a few drops of phenolphthalein indicator; the metal floats, melts, moves about, produces a hissing sound, and turns the solution red, demonstrating the high reactivity of an active metal with water.
objectives: Observe and explain the five characteristic phenomena
Recognize that a strong alkali (sodium hydroxide) is produced
Understand why sodium metal must be stored under oil

iron-rusting.title: Investigation of the Conditions Required for Iron Rusting
iron-rusting.description: Iron nails are exposed simultaneously to dry air, moist air, and water from which air has been excluded; the degree of rusting in each case is compared to establish that both water and oxygen are necessary for corrosion.
objectives: Identify the conditions necessary for iron to rust
Understand the principles of corrosion prevention
Design and evaluate a controlled comparative experiment

aluminum-acid-base.title: Investigation of the Amphoteric Nature of Aluminium
aluminum-acid-base.description: Aluminium strips are placed separately in hydrochloric acid and in sodium hydroxide solution; hydrogen gas is evolved in both cases, demonstrating that aluminium reacts with both acids and bases.
objectives: Recognize the amphoteric character of aluminium
Compare the rates of gas evolution in acidic and alkaline conditions
Write the chemical equations for both types of reaction

magnesium-burning.title: Combustion of Magnesium Ribbon
magnesium-burning.description: Igniting magnesium ribbon produces an intense white light and yields white magnesium oxide, illustrating a highly exothermic oxidation reaction.
objectives: Observe the phenomena of combustion
Identify magnesium oxide as a product
Understand the concept of an exothermic reaction

thermite-reaction.title: Thermite Reaction
thermite-reaction.description: Aluminium powder reacts vigorously with iron(III) oxide at high temperature to produce iron and aluminium oxide, demonstrating a strongly exothermic displacement reaction and its practical applications.
objectives: Recognise the thermite reaction and its characteristic features
Understand its application in industrial welding
Follow safe laboratory procedures during the demonstration

metal-displacement-series.title: Hydrometallurgical Extraction of Copper
metal-displacement-series.description: Iron displaces copper from a copper(II) sulfate solution, simulating the ancient hydrometallurgical process and illustrating the principles underlying metal extraction.
objectives: Understand the principles of hydrometallurgy
Recover metallic copper from solution
Connect the experiment to its historical and cultural context

aluminum-oxide-film.title: Protective Role of the Oxide Film on Aluminium
aluminum-oxide-film.description: Comparing the reaction rates of polished and unpolished aluminium strips in hydrochloric acid demonstrates how the dense, adherent oxide film protects the underlying metal.
objectives: Recognise the protective function of the oxide film on aluminium
Compare reaction rates under different surface conditions
Relate the findings to the corrosion resistance of aluminium products

fe3-scn-coloring.title: Detection of Iron(III) Ions with Thiocyanate
fe3-scn-coloring.description: Adding potassium thiocyanate to an iron(III) chloride solution produces an intense blood-red colour, providing a sensitive qualitative test for Fe³⁺.
objectives: Master the qualitative test for Fe³⁺ using thiocyanate
Observe the characteristic blood-red coloration
Recognise the role of coordinate bond formation in the colour response

copper-ammonia-complex.title: Formation of the Copper–Ammonia Complex Ion
copper-ammonia-complex.description: Adding aqueous ammonia dropwise to a copper(II) sulfate solution first produces a pale-blue precipitate, which then dissolves to give a deep-blue copper–ammonia solution.
objectives: Observe the sequential precipitation and dissolution of the copper hydroxide intermediate
Identify the copper–ammonia complex ion as the product
Understand the concept of coordination equilibrium

fe3-equilibrium-shift.title: Equilibrium Shift in the Iron–Thiocyanate System
fe3-equilibrium-shift.description: Varying the concentration of iron(III) ions or thiocyanate ions in the blood-red iron–thiocyanate solution causes the colour intensity to change, providing direct evidence for Le Chatelier's principle.
objectives: Understand the dynamic nature of chemical equilibrium
Verify the effect of concentration changes on equilibrium position
Perform qualitative analysis based on colour intensity

phenol-fecl3-coloring.title: Colorimetric Detection of Phenol
phenol-fecl3-coloring.description: Adding iron(III) chloride to a phenol solution produces a violet coloration, serving as the characteristic test for the phenolic hydroxyl group.
objectives: Master the colorimetric test for phenol using iron(III) chloride
Observe the characteristic violet coloration
Recognise the distinctive chemical properties of phenol

silver-ammonia-prep.title: Preparation of Silver-Ammonia Solution
silver-ammonia-prep.description: Aqueous ammonia is added dropwise to silver nitrate until the precipitate just dissolves, yielding a silver-ammonia solution (Tollens' reagent) for the detection of aldehyde groups.
objectives: Prepare a silver-ammonia solution
Understand coordination dissolution
Lay the groundwork for the silver mirror reaction

diammine-silver-test.title: Complexometric Titration of Calcium and Magnesium Ions in Hard Water
diammine-silver-test.description: In an ammonia–ammonium chloride buffer at pH≈10, calcium and magnesium ions in a water sample are titrated with a standard EDTA solution using Eriochrome Black T as the indicator; the endpoint is reached when the solution changes from wine-red to pure blue.
objectives: Master complexometric titration
Determine water hardness
Identify the colour-change endpoint

cobalt-chloride-equilibrium.title: Colour Equilibrium of Cobalt(II) Chloride
cobalt-chloride-equilibrium.description: The interconversion between pink and blue in a cobalt(II) chloride solution upon dilution with water and upon heating is observed, illustrating the shift of coordination equilibrium.
objectives: Understand coordination equilibrium
Observe the reversible colour change
Understand equilibrium shifts

prussian-blue.title: Formation of Prussian Blue
prussian-blue.description: Ferrous ions react with potassium hexacyanoferrate(III) to form a blue precipitate; this reaction introduces the classical pigment Prussian blue and serves as a test for ferrous ions.
objectives: Become acquainted with Prussian blue
Test for ferrous ions
Connect the reaction to the history of pigments

ester-synthesis.title: Preparation of Ethyl Acetate
ester-synthesis.description: Acetic acid and ethanol undergo esterification in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid as a catalyst, producing ethyl acetate, which has a characteristic fruity odour.
objectives: Master the esterification reaction
Understand catalysis and dehydration
Recognise the reversibility of the reaction

silver-mirror.title: Silver Mirror Reaction
silver-mirror.description: Acetaldehyde is heated with a silver-ammonia solution in a water bath, depositing a bright silver mirror on the inner wall of the test tube and demonstrating the reducing property of the aldehyde group.
objectives: Master the test for aldehyde groups
Observe the formation of a silver mirror
Understand reducing properties

glucose-fehling.title: Reaction of Glucose with Freshly Prepared Copper(II) Hydroxide
glucose-fehling.description: Glucose is heated with freshly prepared copper(II) hydroxide, producing a brick-red precipitate of copper(I) oxide, which serves as a test for the aldehyde group in glucose.
objectives: Test for glucose
Observe the brick-red precipitate
Connect the reaction to the clinical detection of diabetes

ethylene-bromine.title: Decolourisation of Bromine Water by Ethylene
ethylene-bromine.description: Ethylene is bubbled into bromine water, causing the orange colour to fade, thereby demonstrating the addition reaction of the carbon–carbon double bond.
objectives: Understand addition reactions
Distinguish saturated from unsaturated compounds
Observe the decolourisation

ethanol-sodium.title: Reaction of Ethanol with Sodium
ethanol-sodium.description: When sodium metal is added to anhydrous ethanol, hydrogen gas is evolved slowly. Comparing this with the vigorous reaction between sodium metal and water illustrates the lower reactivity of the hydroxyl hydrogen in alcohols.
objectives: Recognise the reactivity of the hydroxyl group
Compare reaction rates between ethanol and water with sodium metal
Test for hydrogen gas

phenol-bromine-water.title: Reaction of Phenol with Bromine Water
phenol-bromine-water.description: Adding bromine water to a phenol solution produces a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol, demonstrating the ring-activating effect of the hydroxyl group on electrophilic aromatic substitution.
objectives: Recognise electrophilic substitution reactions
Observe the formation of a white precipitate
Understand how substituent groups influence aromatic reactivity

starch-iodine-test.title: Detection of Starch with Iodine
starch-iodine-test.description: Iodine solution is used to test for the presence of starch in food samples; a blue-black colouration confirms the presence of starch, linking the test to the analysis of food composition.
objectives: Perform a qualitative test for starch
Observe the characteristic colour change
Relate the test to everyday food science

sucrose-hydrolysis.title: Hydrolysis of Sucrose
sucrose-hydrolysis.description: Sucrose is hydrolysed to glucose and fructose under dilute sulfuric acid catalysis; the hydrolysis products are subsequently confirmed using Tollens' reagent (silver–ammonia solution).
objectives: Understand hydrolysis reactions of disaccharides
Appreciate the role of acid catalysis
Identify the hydrolysis products using Tollens' reagent

ethanol-oxidation-copper.title: Catalytic Oxidation of Ethanol
ethanol-oxidation-copper.description: A heated copper wire catalyses the oxidation of ethanol to acetaldehyde; the copper wire alternates between black (copper(II) oxide) and red (copper), illustrating the catalytic cycle of the oxidation of alcohols.
objectives: Understand catalytic oxidation of alcohols
Observe the colour changes of the copper wire
Explain the regeneration of the catalyst

soap-saponification.title: Preparation of Soap (Saponification)
soap-saponification.description: Fats and oils are heated with sodium hydroxide solution and undergo base hydrolysis to yield sodium salts of higher fatty acids (soap) and glycerol.
objectives: Understand the saponification reaction
Practise the salting-out procedure
Relate the process to the industrial production of daily-use chemicals

solubility-measurement.title: Determination of the Solubility of Potassium Nitrate
solubility-measurement.description: The solubility of potassium nitrate is determined at various temperatures and the results are used to construct a solubility curve, investigating the effect of temperature on solubility.
objectives: Understand the concept of solubility
Investigate the effect of temperature on solubility
Plot and interpret a solubility curve

dissolution-heat.title: Endothermic and Exothermic Dissolution Processes
dissolution-heat.description: The temperature changes accompanying the dissolution of sodium hydroxide, ammonium nitrate, and sodium chloride in water are compared, illustrating the thermal effects associated with dissolution.
objectives: Understand the concept of enthalpy of dissolution
Distinguish between endothermic and exothermic dissolution
Relate the observations to the working principles of instant heat packs and instant cold packs

neutralization-enthalpy.title: Determination of Neutralization Enthalpy
neutralization-enthalpy.description: Measure the enthalpy change of the neutralization reaction between a strong acid and a strong base, and develop an understanding of exothermic reactions and conservation of energy.
objectives: Determine the enthalpy of neutralization
Understand the concept of reaction enthalpy
Analyze sources of experimental error

endothermic-reaction.title: Investigation of Endothermic Reactions
endothermic-reaction.description: Mix barium hydroxide crystals with ammonium chloride solid and observe the sharp drop in temperature, illustrating a typical endothermic reaction.
objectives: Recognize the characteristics of endothermic reactions
Observe the formation of ice during the reaction
Understand the relationship between chemical reactions and energy changes

reaction-rate-temperature.title: Effect of Temperature on Reaction Rate
reaction-rate-temperature.description: Compare the time required for a cloudy precipitate to appear when sodium thiosulfate reacts with dilute sulfuric acid at different temperatures, and investigate how temperature affects reaction rate.
objectives: Investigate the effect of temperature on reaction rate
Apply the controlled-variable method
Record and compare reaction times

concentration-rate.title: Effect of Concentration on Reaction Rate
concentration-rate.description: Compare the rate of gas evolution when hydrochloric acid of different concentrations reacts with magnesium ribbon of equal size, and develop a quantitative understanding of how concentration affects reaction rate.
objectives: Investigate the effect of concentration on reaction rate
Apply the controlled-variable method
Record and compare rates of gas evolution

catalyst-rate.title: Effect of a Catalyst on Reaction Rate
catalyst-rate.description: Compare the rate of oxygen evolution from the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide with and without manganese(IV) oxide, and recognize that a catalyst significantly accelerates a reaction.
objectives: Understand the role of a catalyst
Compare reaction rates under different conditions
Develop a basic understanding of catalytic mechanisms

surface-area-rate.title: Effect of Surface Area on Reaction Rate
surface-area-rate.description: Compare the reaction rate of lumped versus powdered calcium carbonate with hydrochloric acid, and recognize the effect of reactant surface area on reaction rate.
objectives: Investigate the effect of contact surface area on reaction rate
Apply the controlled-variable method
Record and compare volumes of gas evolved

chemical-equilibrium-temp.title: Effect of Temperature on Chemical Equilibrium
chemical-equilibrium-temp.description: Observe the color changes in an equilibrium system of nitrogen dioxide and dinitrogen tetroxide when placed alternately in hot and cold water, and recognize how temperature shifts a chemical equilibrium.
objectives: Understand the concept of equilibrium shift
Observe color changes as evidence of equilibrium displacement
Understand Le Chatelier's principle

instant-cold-pack.title: Principle of Instant Cold Packs
instant-cold-pack.description: Prepare a simple cold compress using the endothermic dissolution of ammonium nitrate, and connect the concept of heat of solution to its practical application in everyday life.
objectives: Apply the concept of endothermic dissolution
Measure the magnitude of temperature decrease
Connect the experiment to the use of medical cold packs

flame-test.title: Flame Test
flame-test.description: A platinum wire is used to introduce different metal salts into a flame, and the characteristic flame colors are observed: sodium yellow, potassium violet, and calcium brick-red.
objectives: Master the technique of the flame test
Identify metal elements by their characteristic flame colors
Connect the underlying principle to the colors produced in fireworks

chloride-identification.title: Qualitative Test for Chloride Ions
chloride-identification.description: Silver nitrate solution and dilute nitric acid are used to test for chloride ions in solution; the formation of a white precipitate confirms their presence.
objectives: Master the procedure for testing chloride ions
Eliminate potential interfering ions
Observe and interpret precipitate formation

sulfate-identification.title: Qualitative Test for Sulfate Ions
sulfate-identification.description: Barium chloride solution and dilute hydrochloric acid are used to test for sulfate ions; the formation of a white precipitate insoluble in acid confirms their presence.
objectives: Master the procedure for testing sulfate ions
Eliminate interference from carbonate ions
Observe and interpret precipitate formation

carbonate-identification.title: Qualitative Test for Carbonate Ions
carbonate-identification.description: Dilute hydrochloric acid and limewater are used to test for carbonate ions; the evolution of a gas that turns limewater milky confirms their presence.
objectives: Master the procedure for testing carbonate ions
Observe gas evolution during the reaction
Identify the evolved gas as CO₂

fe3-identification.title: Test for Iron(III) Ions
fe3-identification.description: Potassium thiocyanate is used to test for iron(III) ions; the appearance of a blood-red coloration in the solution confirms their presence and demonstrates a sensitive qualitative test.
objectives: Master the procedure for testing Fe³⁺
Observe the characteristic color reaction
Distinguish between different oxidation states of iron

ammonium-identification.title: Test for Ammonium Ions
ammonium-identification.description: An ammonium salt is warmed with a base, releasing ammonia gas, which turns moist red litmus paper blue, thereby confirming the presence of ammonium ions.
objectives: Master the procedure for testing ammonium ions
Identify the evolved ammonia gas
Understand the conditions required for gas evolution

copper-identification.title: Test for Copper(II) Ions
copper-identification.description: Sodium hydroxide solution is added to a solution containing copper(II) ions, producing a blue precipitate and confirming their presence.
objectives: Master the procedure for testing copper(II) ions
Observe the formation of the characteristic blue precipitate
Associate solution color with the identity of dissolved ions

copper-electrolysis.title: Electrolysis of Copper(II) Sulfate Solution
copper-electrolysis.description: During the electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate solution, copper is deposited at the cathode and oxygen is evolved at the anode, illustrating the principles of electrolysis and electrode reactions.
objectives: Understand the principles of electrolysis
Write the electrode half-reactions
Observe the phenomena occurring at each electrode

copper-zinc-cell.title: Copper-Zinc Galvanic Cell
copper-zinc-cell.description: A galvanic cell is assembled using a copper strip, a zinc strip, and dilute sulfuric acid; the resulting current deflects the galvanometer, demonstrating the conversion of chemical energy into electrical energy.
objectives: Understand the operating principle of a galvanic cell
Identify the positive and negative electrodes
Understand the mechanism of energy conversion

electroplating-copper.title: Copper Electroplating
electroplating-copper.description: The object to be plated is used as the cathode and copper as the anode in a copper(II) sulfate solution; the experiment illustrates the principle and practical application of electroplating.
objectives: Understand the principle of electroplating
Control the current during the plating process
Observe the quality and appearance of the deposited layer

iron-electrochemical-corrosion.title: Electrochemical Corrosion of Iron
iron-electrochemical-corrosion.description: Brine is used to simulate the oxygen-absorption corrosion of steel, and potassium hexacyanoferrate(III) indicator is employed to reveal the corrosion microcell.
objectives: Understand the mechanism of oxygen-absorption corrosion
Understand the structure and function of a corrosion microcell
Connect experimental observations to practical metal protection

sacrificial-anode.title: Sacrificial Anode Protection
sacrificial-anode.description: A zinc block is connected to an iron article to retard the corrosion of iron, illustrating the cathodic protection principle of the sacrificial anode method.
objectives: Understand the principle of cathodic protection
Compare corrosion rates under different conditions
Connect the method to corrosion prevention in marine engineering

gas-volume-measurement.title: Measurement of Gas Volume
gas-volume-measurement.description: The water-displacement method is used to measure the volume of carbon dioxide evolved from the reaction of calcium carbonate with hydrochloric acid, providing practice in quantitative gas measurement.
objectives: Master the water-displacement gas-collection technique
Read gas volumes accurately from graduated apparatus
Calculate the amount of substance involved in the reaction

crystallization-purification.title: Purification of Crude Salt
crystallization-purification.description: Crude table salt (sodium chloride) containing sand and mud is purified by successive dissolution, filtration, and evaporative crystallization, developing core skills in the separation of mixtures.
objectives: Master the filtration technique
Master evaporative crystallization
Understand the general strategy for purifying a mixture

electrolysis-water.title: Electrolysis of Water
electrolysis-water.description: Water is electrolysed in dilute sulfuric acid; hydrogen gas is produced at the cathode and oxygen at the anode, with a volume ratio of approximately 2∶1.
objectives: Verify the elemental composition of water
Write the electrode half-reactions
Measure and interpret the volume ratio of the product gases

electrolysis-nacl-solution.title: Electrolysis of Saturated Brine
electrolysis-nacl-solution.description: Electrolysis of a saturated sodium chloride solution yields hydrogen gas at the cathode and chlorine at the anode, while sodium hydroxide accumulates in the catholyte.
objectives: Understand the basis of the chlor-alkali industrial process
Write the electrode half-reactions
Test for the alkalinity of the cathodic solution

electrolysis-cucl2-solution.title: Electrolysis of Copper(II) Chloride Solution
electrolysis-cucl2-solution.description: Electrolysis of a copper(II) chloride solution deposits red copper at the cathode and releases yellow-green chlorine at the anode, illustrating how electrolysis products are identified.
objectives: Identify the products of electrolysis
Write electrode reactions
Observe the phenomena at both electrodes

copper-refining-electrolysis.title: Electrolytic Refining of Copper
copper-refining-electrolysis.description: Using crude copper as the anode and pure copper as the cathode in a copper(II) sulfate solution, the anode dissolves while high-purity copper is deposited at the cathode.
objectives: Understand the principle of electrolytic refining
Recognise the formation of anode slime
Write electrode reactions

electroplating-silver.title: Silver Electroplating
electroplating-silver.description: The object to be plated serves as the cathode and silver as the anode in a silver-salt solution, demonstrating how an electroplated coating is formed.
objectives: Understand the principle of electroplating
Control the thickness of the deposited layer
Recognise practical applications of silver plating

fruit-battery.title: Fruit Battery
fruit-battery.description: Inserting a copper strip and a zinc strip into a lemon or similar fruit forms a galvanic cell capable of lighting a small bulb or deflecting a galvanometer.
objectives: Understand the components of a galvanic cell
Identify the positive and negative electrodes
Understand the conversion of chemical energy to electrical energy

daniell-cell.title: Daniell Cell
daniell-cell.description: A zinc strip immersed in zinc sulfate and a copper strip immersed in copper(II) sulfate are connected by a salt bridge to form a classic galvanic cell, allowing measurement of the electromotive force.
objectives: Understand the two-electrolyte galvanic cell
Understand the function of the salt bridge
Measure the electromotive force

iron-carbon-galvanic-corrosion.title: Iron–Carbon Galvanic Corrosion
iron-carbon-galvanic-corrosion.description: Iron and carbon form a galvanic cell in dilute hydrochloric acid, with iron acting as the negative electrode and dissolving at an accelerated rate, illustrating hydrogen-evolution corrosion of steel.
objectives: Understand hydrogen-evolution corrosion
Understand the micro-galvanic cell mechanism
Compare corrosion rates under different conditions

oxygen-absorption-corrosion.title: Investigation of Oxygen-Absorption Corrosion of Steel
oxygen-absorption-corrosion.description: Iron nails placed in neutral brine cause the liquid level in the delivery tube to rise after some time, confirming that oxygen-absorption corrosion consumes oxygen.
objectives: Understand oxygen-absorption corrosion
Compare oxygen-absorption corrosion with hydrogen-evolution corrosion
Connect findings to methods of metal protection

impressed-current-protection.title: Impressed-Current Cathodic Protection
impressed-current-protection.description: The iron object to be protected is connected to the negative terminal of a direct current power supply, with an inert anode completing the circuit, preventing corrosion of the iron.
objectives: Understand impressed-current cathodic protection
Compare this method with the sacrificial anode method
Connect findings to pipeline corrosion prevention

dry-cell-dissection.title: Investigating the Structure of a Dry Cell
dry-cell-dissection.description: Disassemble a zinc-manganese dry cell to examine the zinc canister (negative electrode), carbon rod (positive electrode), and electrolyte paste, thereby understanding the operating principle of a primary battery.
objectives: Identify the components of a dry cell
Distinguish the materials of the positive and negative electrodes
Understand the principle of a primary battery

electrolysis-electrode-products.title: Investigating Electrode Products in Inert-Electrode Electrolysis
electrolysis-electrode-products.description: Electrolyse separate solutions of sodium sulfate and potassium nitrate using inert electrodes; test the acid-base changes at each electrode with litmus, and derive the discharge sequence of ions.
objectives: Derive the ion discharge sequence
Test the products at each electrode
Write the electrode reaction equations

conductivity-electrolyte.title: Electrical Conductivity of Electrolyte Solutions
conductivity-electrolyte.description: Use an electrical conductivity apparatus to compare the conductivities of sodium chloride solution, hydrochloric acid, and sucrose solution, and thereby distinguish electrolytes from non-electrolytes.
objectives: Distinguish electrolytes from non-electrolytes
Understand electrical conduction by ions
Compare the brightness of the indicator bulb across samples

molten-salt-electrolysis.title: Electrolysis of Molten Sodium Chloride
molten-salt-electrolysis.description: Electrolyse molten sodium chloride at high temperature; sodium metal is deposited at the cathode and chlorine is evolved at the anode, illustrating the smelting of reactive metals.
objectives: Understand the electrolysis of a molten salt
Understand the industrial production of sodium metal
Write the electrode reaction equations

aluminum-electrolysis.title: Production of Aluminium by Electrolysis of Aluminium Oxide
aluminum-electrolysis.description: Electrolyse molten aluminium oxide with cryolite as a flux; aluminium is deposited at the cathode while the carbon anode is oxidised, illustrating the industrial smelting of aluminium.
objectives: Understand the industrial production of aluminium
Understand the role of cryolite
Write the electrode reaction equations

lead-acid-battery.title: Investigating the Lead-Acid Storage Battery
lead-acid-battery.description: Examine the changes in electrode material composition and sulfuric acid concentration during the discharge and charge cycles of a lead-acid storage battery, thereby understanding the principle of a secondary battery.
objectives: Understand the nature of a secondary battery
Understand the principles of charging and discharging
Relate the findings to the automotive lead-acid battery

concentration-cell.title: Concentration Cell
concentration-cell.description: Insert two silver electrodes into silver nitrate solutions of different concentrations and connect them with a salt bridge; the resulting potential difference illustrates the principle of a concentration cell.
objectives: Understand the nature of a concentration cell
Understand the effect of concentration on electrode potential
Measure the electromotive force of the cell

electrolysis-copper-anode.title: Comparing Active and Inert Electrodes in Electrolysis
electrolysis-copper-anode.description: Compare the electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate solution using a copper anode against that using a carbon anode, and thereby understand how an active electrode participates directly in the electrode reaction.
objectives: Distinguish inert from active electrodes
Compare the anodic reactions in each case
Write the electrode half-reaction equations

faraday-electrolysis-quantitative.title: Faraday Electrolysis Quantitative Experiment
faraday-electrolysis-quantitative.description: Electrolyse a copper(II) sulfate solution and measure the mass gained at the cathode to verify that the mass of copper deposited is proportional to the quantity of charge passed.
objectives: Verify Faraday's law of electrolysis
Measure the amount of deposited substance quantitatively
Calculate the number of electrons transferred

galvanic-metal-comparison.title: Identifying the Electrodes of a Galvanic Cell
galvanic-metal-comparison.description: Construct galvanic cells using pairs of different metals with dilute sulfuric acid, and determine the more active metal as the negative electrode by observing the deflection of the galvanometer.
objectives: Identify the positive and negative electrodes
Relate electrode polarity to the activity series of metals
Understand the direction of electron flow

hydrogen-oxygen-fuel-cell.title: Hydrogen–Oxygen Fuel Cell
hydrogen-oxygen-fuel-cell.description: Construct a fuel cell using hydrogen gas as the negative electrode and oxygen as the positive electrode in aqueous potassium hydroxide solution, and use it to light a small lamp.
objectives: Recognise the operating principle of a fuel cell
Write the electrode half-reactions
Understand the high efficiency and clean nature of fuel cells

electrochemical-etching.title: Electrochemical Etching of Metals
electrochemical-etching.description: Connect the metal workpiece as the anode and pass current through a sodium chloride electrolyte to dissolve the surface selectively, achieving electrochemical machining by etching.
objectives: Understand anodic dissolution
Recognise the principle of electrolytic machining
Control the region subjected to etching

anodizing-aluminum.title: Anodising of Aluminium
anodizing-aluminum.description: Connect an aluminium workpiece as the anode and pass current through dilute sulfuric acid; a dense aluminium oxide film forms on the surface, improving corrosion resistance and receptivity to colouring.
objectives: Recognise the process of anodic oxidation
Understand how the oxide film grows with time
Connect the process to industrial surface treatment of aluminium

silver-electrolytic-cleaning.title: Electrochemical Reduction of Tarnished Silverware
silver-electrolytic-cleaning.description: Place tarnished silverware together with aluminium foil in a hot sodium carbonate solution to form a galvanic cell, reducing silver sulfide back to silver.
objectives: Recognise the reducing action of a galvanic cell
Understand the principle behind the removal of tarnish
Connect the method to everyday applications

electrolysis-ki-solution.title: Electrolysis of Potassium Iodide Solution
electrolysis-ki-solution.description: Electrolyse a potassium iodide solution; iodine produced at the anode turns starch blue, while hydrogen gas evolved at the cathode makes phenolphthalein turn red, providing a clear visual demonstration of the products at each electrode.
objectives: Identify the products of electrolysis at each electrode
Test for iodine produced at the anode
Confirm the alkaline conditions at the cathode

silver-ammonia-complex-dissolve.title: Dissolution of Silver Chloride in Aqueous Ammonia and Regeneration with Nitric Acid
silver-ammonia-complex-dissolve.description: A white precipitate of silver chloride dissolves in aqueous ammonia to form the diamminesilver(I) complex ion; addition of nitric acid then causes the precipitate to reform.
objectives: Recognise complex-ion formation as a mechanism for dissolution
Understand the stability of the complex ion formed
Observe the dissolution and regeneration of the precipitate

copper-ammonia-deep-blue.title: Copper(II) Sulfate with Excess Aqueous Ammonia
copper-ammonia-deep-blue.description: Adding aqueous ammonia to a copper(II) sulfate solution first produces a pale blue precipitate, which dissolves in excess aqueous ammonia to form the deep blue tetraamminecopper(II) complex ion.
objectives: Observe the sequential formation and dissolution of a precipitate
Identify the tetraamminecopper(II) complex ion
Understand coordination equilibrium

agi-ammonia-insoluble.title: Insolubility of Silver Iodide in Aqueous Ammonia
agi-ammonia-insoluble.description: A comparative study of the solubility of silver chloride, silver bromide, and silver iodide in aqueous ammonia, illustrating the trend in solubility products of the silver halides.
objectives: Compare the solubility of silver halides in aqueous ammonia
Relate solubility to solubility-product constants
Understand competition between coordination and precipitation equilibria

nickel-dimethylglyoxime.title: Detection of Nickel with Dimethylglyoxime
nickel-dimethylglyoxime.description: In weakly alkaline solution, nickel(II) ions react with dimethylglyoxime to form a bright red chelate precipitate, providing a characteristic test for nickel.
objectives: Recognise chelate colour formation
Master the characteristic test for nickel
Understand the role of selective reagents

fe3-salicylic-acid.title: Colour Reaction of Iron(III) with Salicylic Acid
fe3-salicylic-acid.description: Iron(III) ions react with salicylic acid to form a violet-red complex whose coordination number and colour vary with pH, making the reaction suitable for colorimetric determination of iron.
objectives: Observe coordination-based colour development
Understand the effect of pH on complex formation
Connect the reaction to colorimetric analysis

cobalt-thiocyanate-test.title: Detection of Cobalt with Ammonium Thiocyanate
cobalt-thiocyanate-test.description: Cobalt(II) ions react with ammonium thiocyanate in acetone to form a blue complex ion, which can be used to detect and identify cobalt.
objectives: Identify the cobalt–thiocyanate complex ion
Master the characteristic test for cobalt
Compare with the iron(III)–thiocyanate colour reaction

tetraamminecopper-crystal.title: Preparation of Tetraamminecopper(II) Sulfate Crystals
tetraamminecopper-crystal.description: Adding ethanol to a copper–ammonia solution reduces the solubility of the complex, causing deep blue tetraamminecopper(II) sulfate crystals to crystallise out.
objectives: Prepare crystals of a coordination compound
Understand crystallisation by reduction of solubility
Recognise the composition of a coordination compound

fe-scn-concentration-color.title: Effect of Concentration on the Colour of the Iron–Thiocyanate Complex
fe-scn-concentration-color.description: Varying the concentration of iron(III) ions or thiocyanate ions changes the depth of the red colour of the iron–thiocyanate complex ion, demonstrating the nature of coordination equilibrium.
objectives: Observe changes in colour intensity
Understand the effect of concentration on equilibrium
Connect observations to quantitative colorimetric analysis

zinc-ammonia-complex.title: Formation of the Tetraamminezinc(II) Complex Ion
zinc-ammonia-complex.description: Adding aqueous ammonia to a zinc sulfate solution first produces a white zinc hydroxide precipitate, which dissolves in excess aqueous ammonia to form the tetraamminezinc(II) complex ion.
objectives: Observe the dissolution of a precipitate in excess ligand
Identify the tetraamminezinc(II) complex ion
Compare zinc–ammonia and copper–ammonia coordination behaviour

aluminum-hydroxide-amphoteric-complex.title: Amphoteric Behaviour and Coordination Chemistry of Aluminium Hydroxide
aluminum-hydroxide-amphoteric-complex.description: Aluminium hydroxide dissolves in both hydrochloric acid and excess sodium hydroxide to form meta-aluminate, illustrating the properties of an amphoteric hydroxide.
objectives: Recognise amphoteric behaviour
Understand dissolution by coordination
Write both types of chemical equations

chromium-color-states.title: The Colourful Coordination States of Chromium
chromium-color-states.description: Observe the reversible orange-to-yellow colour change of potassium dichromate under acidic and basic conditions, and understand the chromate–dichromate equilibrium.
objectives: Observe the reversible colour change
Understand the chromate equilibrium
Recognise the effect of pH

copper-chloride-complex-color.title: Colour Change of the Chlorocuprate Complex Ion
copper-chloride-complex-color.description: Addition of concentrated hydrochloric acid to a copper(II) sulfate solution produces a yellow-green chlorocuprate complex ion; subsequent dilution restores the blue colour.
objectives: Observe coordination-dependent colour
Understand ligand exchange
Connect to the cobalt(II) chloride equilibrium

starch-iodine-complex.title: Colour Reaction of the Starch–Iodine Complex
starch-iodine-complex.description: Iodine forms a blue inclusion complex with starch; the colour disappears on heating and reappears on cooling, demonstrating a reversible colour reaction.
objectives: Observe the blue inclusion complex
Understand the reversible colour reaction
Connect to the detection of iodine

silver-ammonia-fresh-prep.title: Correct Preparation of Silver–Ammonia Solution
silver-ammonia-fresh-prep.description: Aqueous ammonia is added dropwise to silver nitrate until the precipitate just dissolves, yielding a clear silver–ammonia solution; the solution must be prepared immediately before use.
objectives: Master the preparation procedure
Understand the requirement for a stoichiometric amount of aqueous ammonia
Recognise that the solution cannot be stored

fe3-fluoride-masking.title: Masking of Iron(III) with Fluoride Ion
fe3-fluoride-masking.description: Addition of sodium fluoride to a blood-red thiocyanato–iron solution produces the more stable fluoroiron complex, causing the red colour to disappear.
objectives: Understand competitive coordination
Recognise the role of a masking agent
Compare the stability of different complexes

copper-edta-complex.title: EDTA Coordination of Copper Ion
copper-edta-complex.description: Addition of EDTA to a blue copper(II) sulfate solution forms the more stable copper–EDTA complex ion, which is employed in complexometric titration.
objectives: Recognise EDTA coordination
Understand 1∶1 complex formation
Connect to complexometric titration

calcium-carbonate-hardness-titration.title: Complexometric Titration of Total Water Hardness
calcium-carbonate-hardness-titration.description: A standard EDTA solution is used to titrate a water sample in the presence of Eriochrome Black T indicator, determining the total calcium and magnesium content and hence the total hardness of the water.
objectives: Determine total water hardness
Master endpoint identification
Calculate the hardness content

nickel-ammonia-complex.title: Formation of the Nickel–Ammonia Complex Ion
nickel-ammonia-complex.description: Adding excess aqueous ammonia to a nickel(II) chloride solution causes the colour to change from green to blue-violet, illustrating the coordination chemistry of nickel.
objectives: Observe the colour change during complex formation
Identify the nickel–ammonia complex ion
Compare nickel–ammonia coordination with copper–ammonia coordination

hexacyanoferrate-color.title: Stability of Hexacyanoferrate Complex Ions
hexacyanoferrate-color.description: Comparing the colours of potassium hexacyanoferrate(II) and potassium hexacyanoferrate(III) solutions illustrates the two cyano-complex ions of iron and their respective oxidation states.
objectives: Distinguish between the two hexacyanoferrate complex ions
Relate each complex ion to the corresponding oxidation state of iron
Understand the stability of complex ions

turnbull-blue.title: Formation of Turnbull's Blue
turnbull-blue.description: Iron(II) ions react with potassium hexacyanoferrate(III) to produce a blue precipitate known as Turnbull's blue, which serves as a qualitative test for iron(II) ions.
objectives: Use the reaction to test for iron(II) ions
Compare Turnbull's blue with Prussian blue
Understand the formation of coordination precipitates

cobalt-ammonia-oxidation.title: Oxidation of the Cobalt–Ammonia Complex Ion
cobalt-ammonia-oxidation.description: The cobalt(II)–ammonia complex ion is oxidised in air to yield the stable orange-yellow cobalt(III)–ammonia complex ion, demonstrating how coordination can stabilise higher oxidation states.
objectives: Observe the colour change accompanying oxidation
Understand how coordination stabilises higher oxidation states
Recognise the properties of cobalt coordination compounds

ferric-phenol-purple.title: Colour Reaction of Iron(III) with Phenol
ferric-phenol-purple.description: Adding iron(III) chloride solution to a phenol solution produces a violet-coloured complex, providing a colour test for phenolic hydroxyl groups and iron(III) ions.
objectives: Observe the characteristic violet colouration
Use the reaction as a test for phenolic hydroxyl groups
Recognise the nature of the iron–phenol complex

ammonium-chloride-hydrolysis.title: Hydrolysis of Ammonium Chloride Solution
ammonium-chloride-hydrolysis.description: The pH of an ammonium chloride solution is measured and the solution is tested with litmus, investigating how the hydrolysis of a salt derived from a strong acid and a weak base produces an acidic solution.
objectives: Understand why a strong-acid–weak-base salt hydrolyses to give an acidic solution
Use indicators to determine the acid–base character of a solution
Write the ionic equation for the hydrolysis of ammonium chloride

washing-soda-alkalinity.title: Alkalinity of Sodium Carbonate Solution
washing-soda-alkalinity.description: Adding phenolphthalein to a sodium carbonate solution produces a red colouration, demonstrating that sodium carbonate is alkaline due to hydrolysis and accounting for its ability to remove grease.
objectives: Understand why a strong-base–weak-acid salt hydrolyses to give an alkaline solution
Observe the colour change of phenolphthalein in an alkaline medium
Connect the alkalinity of sodium carbonate to its everyday use as a cleaning agent

acetate-salt-basicity.title: Investigation of the Alkalinity of Sodium Acetate Solution
acetate-salt-basicity.description: Sodium acetate, prepared by reacting acetic acid with sodium hydroxide, turns phenolphthalein red when the indicator is added to the resulting solution, confirming that a salt derived from a weak acid and a strong base hydrolyses to give an alkaline solution.
objectives: Understand the hydrolysis behaviour of a weak-acid–strong-base salt
Determine the properties of the product formed after neutralisation
Write the hydrolysis equation for sodium acetate

methyl-orange-transition-range.title: Determination of the Transition Range of Methyl Orange
methyl-orange-transition-range.description: The ratio of hydrochloric acid to sodium hydroxide is varied dropwise, and the gradual color change of methyl orange from red to yellow is observed to establish its transition range.
objectives: Recognize the transition range of methyl orange
Understand the underlying mechanism of indicator color change
Learn to select an appropriate indicator based on pH

phenolphthalein-transition-range.title: Observation of the Transition Range of Phenolphthalein
phenolphthalein-transition-range.description: The color change of phenolphthalein from colorless to red is observed in sodium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid solutions of varying pH, illustrating that phenolphthalein changes color in the weakly alkaline region.
objectives: Identify the transition range of phenolphthalein
Compare the applicable conditions of different indicators
Determine the acid-base character of a solution

strong-acid-weak-base-titration.title: Titration of a Weak Base with a Strong Acid
strong-acid-weak-base-titration.description: A standard hydrochloric acid solution is used to titrate aqueous ammonia; because the equivalence point is slightly acidic, methyl orange is selected as the indicator, illustrating the choice of indicator for strong-acid–weak-base titrations.
objectives: Understand why the equivalence point of a strong-acid–weak-base titration lies on the acidic side
Master the basis for indicator selection
Calculate the concentration of aqueous ammonia

weak-acid-strong-base-titration.title: Indicator Selection for the Titration of a Weak Acid
weak-acid-strong-base-titration.description: Sodium hydroxide is used to titrate acetic acid; because the equivalence point is slightly alkaline, phenolphthalein is chosen as the indicator, illustrating the basis for indicator selection in weak-acid–strong-base titrations.
objectives: Recognize why the equivalence point of a weak-acid–strong-base titration lies on the alkaline side
Perform burette operations according to standard technique
Analyze end-point errors

back-titration-carbonate.title: Determination of Calcium Carbonate by Back-Titration
back-titration-carbonate.description: Calcium carbonate is first allowed to react with an excess of hydrochloric acid; the remaining acid is then back-titrated with sodium hydroxide using methyl orange to signal the end point, enabling calculation of the calcium carbonate content.
objectives: Understand the principle of back-titration and the situations in which it applies
Carry out a two-step quantitative calculation
Analyze sources of error

phosphoric-acid-stepwise-titration.title: Stepwise Titration of Phosphoric Acid
phosphoric-acid-stepwise-titration.description: Sodium hydroxide is used to titrate phosphoric acid; methyl orange and phenolphthalein are employed in turn to observe two distinct breaks in the titration curve, illustrating the stepwise neutralization of a triprotic weak acid.
objectives: Understand the stepwise ionization and neutralization of a polyprotic weak acid
Identify the two breaks in a titration curve
Calculate the volume of sodium hydroxide consumed at each neutralization stage

carbonate-double-indicator.title: Determination of Sodium Carbonate by the Double-Indicator Method
carbonate-double-indicator.description: Hydrochloric acid is used to titrate sodium carbonate in two stages; phenolphthalein and methyl orange signal the first and second end points in succession, allowing the amount of sodium carbonate neutralized at each stage to be determined.
objectives: Understand the principle of stepwise titration using two indicators
Distinguish the products formed at each end point
Calculate the sodium carbonate content

common-ion-ammonia.title: Investigation of the Common-Ion Effect
common-ion-ammonia.description: When ammonium chloride is added to aqueous ammonia that has been rendered pink by phenolphthalein, the color fades, demonstrating that the common-ion effect suppresses the ionization of aqueous ammonia.
objectives: Understand the common-ion effect
Analyze the direction of shift in the ionization equilibrium
Explain the reason for the fading of color

ammonia-weak-base.title: Weak Alkalinity of Aqueous Ammonia
ammonia-weak-base.description: Compare the pH of aqueous ammonia and sodium hydroxide solution at equal concentrations to understand that aqueous ammonia is only partially ionized and therefore weakly alkaline.
objectives: Distinguish between strong and weak bases
Understand the partial ionization of weak electrolytes
Explain the observed difference in pH

so2-alkali-absorption.title: Reaction of Sulfur Dioxide with Alkali
so2-alkali-absorption.description: Pass sulfur dioxide into sodium hydroxide solution and confirm its absorption; use litmus to verify that an acidic oxide undergoes neutralization with a base.
objectives: Recognize the reaction between acidic oxides and bases
Understand the principle of tail-gas absorption
Write the corresponding chemical equations

carbonic-acid-acidity.title: Investigation of the Acidity of Carbonic Acid
carbonic-acid-acidity.description: Bubble carbon dioxide through distilled water containing litmus to produce a red coloration, then heat the solution to observe decolorization, demonstrating that carbonic acid is a weak and thermally unstable acid.
objectives: Understand that an acid anhydride dissolved in water forms an acid
Recognize the weak acidity and instability of carbonic acid
Explain the decolorization observed upon heating

magnesium-oxide-acid.title: Reaction of Magnesium Oxide with Hydrochloric Acid
magnesium-oxide-acid.description: Dissolve white magnesium oxide in dilute hydrochloric acid to form a magnesium chloride solution, illustrating the neutralization reaction between a basic oxide and an acid.
objectives: Recognize the reaction between basic oxides and acids
Observe the dissolution of a solid reactant
Write the corresponding chemical equations

bicarbonate-acid-salt.title: Properties of Sodium Bicarbonate as an Acid Salt
bicarbonate-acid-salt.description: Measure the weakly alkaline pH of a sodium bicarbonate solution and observe gas evolution upon addition of hydrochloric acid, in order to understand the hydrolysis and amphoteric character of an acid salt.
objectives: Understand the acid-base nature of an acid-salt solution
Observe gas evolution during the reaction with an acid
Compare the properties of sodium bicarbonate and sodium carbonate

dilution-ionization-degree.title: Dilution and Degree of Ionization
dilution-ionization-degree.description: Progressively dilute acetic acid with distilled water while measuring pH at each step; observe that the degree of ionization increases as concentration decreases, illustrating the shift in the weak-acid ionization equilibrium.
objectives: Understand the relationship between pH and degree of ionization
Analyze the effect of dilution on ionization equilibrium
Explain the behavior of a weak acid upon dilution

h2-flammability-purity.title: Purity Testing and Combustibility of Hydrogen Gas
h2-flammability-purity.description: Generate hydrogen gas by reacting zinc granules with dilute hydrochloric acid; collect a sample in a small test tube and test for purity — a sharp pop confirms purity — then ignite the pure gas and observe the pale-blue flame.
objectives: Master the procedure for testing the purity of hydrogen gas
Observe the pale-blue flame produced by the quiet combustion of hydrogen gas
Understand why purity must be verified before igniting any combustible gas

h2-reduce-cuo.title: Reduction of Copper(II) Oxide by Hydrogen Gas
h2-reduce-cuo.description: Pass a stream of dry hydrogen gas over heated black copper(II) oxide; observe the solid turning red and water droplets forming at the mouth of the test tube, confirming the reducing property of hydrogen gas.
objectives: Verify the reducing property of hydrogen gas
Observe the color change as copper(II) oxide is reduced to copper
Follow the correct operational sequence: begin gas flow before heating, and withdraw the heat source before stopping the gas flow

h2-from-aluminum.title: Preparation of Hydrogen Gas from Aluminium and Sodium Hydroxide Solution
h2-from-aluminum.description: Aluminium strip is reacted with sodium hydroxide solution to generate hydrogen gas, demonstrating that reactive metals can react with both acids and strong alkalis to evolve hydrogen.
objectives: Master the preparation of hydrogen gas by reacting a metal with an alkali
Compare the reactions of aluminium with acids and with alkalis
Consolidate the technique of collecting hydrogen gas by water displacement

o2-from-kmno4.title: Preparation of Oxygen Gas by Thermal Decomposition of Potassium Permanganate
o2-from-kmno4.description: Potassium permanganate is heated to produce oxygen gas; students practise the apparatus setup for heating a solid and collecting the gas by water displacement, and verify the product using a glowing wooden splint.
objectives: Master the preparation of oxygen gas by heating a solid
Understand why the test tube mouth is inclined slightly downward and the role of the cotton wool plug
Learn to collect and identify oxygen gas by the water-displacement method

o2-iron-combustion.title: Combustion of Iron Wire in Oxygen
o2-iron-combustion.description: Oxygen is generated by the catalytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide over manganese(IV) oxide; an iron wire attached to a deflagrating spoon is lowered into a gas collection bottle, where vigorous sparking and formation of a black solid are observed.
objectives: Verify the combustion-supporting property of oxygen
Observe the vigorous combustion of iron in pure oxygen
Understand why water or fine sand is placed at the bottom of the gas collection bottle to prevent cracking

o2-magnesium-combustion.title: Ignition of Magnesium Ribbon in Self-Prepared Oxygen
o2-magnesium-combustion.description: Oxygen is prepared by the manganese(IV) oxide-catalysed decomposition of hydrogen peroxide; a piece of magnesium ribbon is ignited and lowered into the gas collection bottle, producing an intense white flash and a white solid product.
objectives: Observe the vigorous combustion of magnesium in oxygen
Recognise the intense white light emitted and the heat released during magnesium combustion
Note the safety precaution of avoiding direct eye contact with the intense light

o2-catalyst-comparison.title: Investigation of Catalysts for the Decomposition of Hydrogen Peroxide
o2-catalyst-comparison.description: Manganese(IV) oxide and copper(II) oxide are added separately to hydrogen peroxide, and the rates of oxygen evolution are compared to investigate the catalytic effectiveness of different substances.
objectives: Understand how a catalyst increases the rate of a reaction
Compare the catalytic effectiveness of manganese(IV) oxide and copper(II) oxide
Appreciate the controlled-variable approach to experimental inquiry

co2-from-sodium-carbonate.title: Preparation of Carbon Dioxide from Sodium Carbonate and Dilute Hydrochloric Acid
co2-from-sodium-carbonate.description: Sodium carbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to generate carbon dioxide rapidly, producing a more vigorous reaction than with lumps of solid carbonate; the gas may be verified by passing it through limewater.
objectives: Master the preparation of carbon dioxide from a carbonate and an acid
Compare the reaction rates of different carbonates with acid
Verify carbon dioxide using limewater

co2-react-naoh.title: Reaction of Carbon Dioxide with Sodium Hydroxide
co2-react-naoh.description: Carbon dioxide is bubbled into sodium hydroxide solution; the resulting decrease in pressure inside the container causes a flexible bottle to collapse inward or produces a fountain effect, providing evidence that a reaction has occurred.
objectives: Verify that carbon dioxide reacts with an alkali
Infer the occurrence of a reaction with no obvious visual sign from an observed change in pressure
Understand the principle by which an alkaline solution absorbs an acidic gas

co2-drying-purification.title: Purification and Drying of Carbon Dioxide
